title: Legal Volume Concession on Late Charges in an Invoice Payoff — Contingency Placement Agreements
content:
A legal volume concession is taken off the late charges that enter the payoff of a past-due fee invoice of an agreement under the Contingency Placement Agreements. It applies by the suits filed under the client's legal forwarding agreement — the client's holding under the Legal Forwarding Agreements that names this contingency agreement — in the 12 months before the payoff: 25 percent for 3 or more suits, 10 percent for 1 or 2 suits, and nothing for none.

**Records read.** The suit-filed entries in the matter history of that legal forwarding agreement, by their dates. A window of a number of months before a date covers the dates after the same day that number of months earlier, up to and including that date; here the window ends on the day of the payoff. The concession turns on the suits counted, not on the legal forwarding agreement's status.

**How it acts.** The concessions that apply are first added into one share, never more than the whole, and the late charges that enter are reduced once by that share; the unpaid amount itself is never reduced. The payoff is the unpaid amount plus the reduced late charges, rounded to the cent once at the end.

## Desk card

| Suits filed under the legal forwarding agreement, 12 months before the payoff | Concession |
|---|---|
| 3 or more | 25 percent |
| 1 or 2 | 10 percent |
| none, or no legal forwarding agreement held | nothing |

## Hypothetical figures

Payoff on 2026-05-14; suits filed on 2025-05-14, 2025-08-02 and 2026-01-19.

- The suit of 2025-05-14 is on the same day 12 months earlier and falls outside the window; 2 suits count, so the concession is 10 percent.
- With a further suit filed on 2026-05-14 itself, 3 suits count: 25 percent.
- On late charges entering of 60.00 USD with only this concession applying: 10 percent leaves 54.00 USD; 25 percent leaves 45.00 USD.
